newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Autoliv sees more car sector restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Autoliv sees more car sector restructuring.

text.p: Swedish car safety equipment maker Autoliv AB managing director Paul Charlety said on Monday restructuring in the industry would continue.

"The increasing competition and the ongoing restructuring will of course continue and will make the situation more difficult for many subcontractors," Charlety said at the company's annual general shareholders' meeting.

"Car manufacturers will...increasingly have fewer and larger subcontractors. In addition car makers will demand that subcontractors take responsibility for developing complete systems, or macrocomponents, i.e. whole parts of the car," he said.
"Subcontractors which cannot meet these demands will be bought up or will disappear altogether," he said.

Charlety said research showed that some 90 percent of all independent companies which made direct deliveries to large European car makers would not exist in the year 2000. These changes were expected to take five years, he said.
Autoliv said last year that it would merge with the car safety equipment unit of U.S. Morton International Inc.
